steps.body: Joining lengths end to end ADDS them: a 34 cm piece and a 25 cm piece make one 59 cm stretch.
steps.narration: Joining lengths end to end ADDS them: a 34 cm piece and a 25 cm piece make one 59 cm stretch.

widget.prompt: Join a 34 cm piece and a 20 cm piece: from 34, two ten-hops for the second piece.

commonLandings.feedback: Two centimeters of the second piece placed — the whole 20 must join.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 34, 2 hops land on 54.
widget.successFeedback: 54 — the second piece laid end to end carries the far end to the joined total.

predict.prompt: Two pieces joined end to end: what does the far end read?
predict.reveal: Each piece pushes the end farther by its full length — the far end accumulates both.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p add lengths.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p add lengths.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

explanationVariants: The far end is the sum.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the lengths up: same starting point, then read what the ends say — joins add, gaps subtract.

widget.prompt: To show a 34 cm piece joined to a 20 cm piece on a number line, what is the drawing?

options.label: Jump 34 then 20 to land on 54
options.feedback: Correct — lengths chain head to tail on the line, and the landing reads the joined total.

options.label: Two dots at 34 and 20 with nothing between
options.feedback: Dots mark positions; joined LENGTHS need jumps laid end to end from zero.

options.label: Start at 34 and jump back 20
options.feedback: Jumping back takes length away — joining pieces sends the second jump forward.

options.label: Start at 20, jump 20
options.feedback: That drawing loses the 34 entirely; both pieces must appear as their own jumps.
